headline: High: shared project/server filesystem plus broad egress make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading workflow errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a shared project directory and n8n can read/write the server filesystem, so A’s generated content can be consumed by B through a shared file bridge. Neither profile shows provenance tracking or isolation by default. This is not merely manual copy-paste; the interaction is built into their storage surfaces.
conditions: IF n8n workflows read files from the same project directory that gpt-engineer writes
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the project directory from the n8n server filesystem
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files into workflows
Add a manual review step before B consumes A’s outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags or signed artifacts between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem read access, while gpt-engineer explicitly handles OPENAI_API_KEY and n8n handles per-credential secrets plus whatever the workflow processes. If shared files or workflow inputs contain secrets, B can move them through integrations and A can expose them to its model backend. The blast radius includes exfiltration of sensitive data.
conditions: IF secrets or sensitive workflow inputs are placed in the shared project/server filesystem
IF n8n workflows send those inputs to external integration nodes or APIs
IF gpt-engineer forwards file contents into its configured model backend
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory
Restrict n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes
Use a separate workspace for generated code and workflow data
Review outbound integrations before enabling them
requires-engineering: add secret redaction before any cross-agent handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write to filesystem locations that overlap via the project directory/server filesystem. gpt-engineer’s self-isolation is none by default, and n8n’s Execute Command node runs on the server. Concurrent writes or command execution can race and corrupt shared state, especially without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or connected filesystem
IF n8n Execute Command or Code nodes modify files that gpt-engineer also writes
IF no external lock or serialization is enforced
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory or container
Disable concurrent execution on shared paths
Avoid n8n Execute Command for shared artifacts
Use file locks or a queue for writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces code/files that n8n can treat as workflow inputs or artifacts, and n8n’s AI Agent node orchestrates downstream tools. If B consumes A’s output without verification, mistakes or malicious instructions can cascade into automated actions. The pair’s default tool-use patterns make this plausible without an explicit safety gate.
conditions: IF n8n workflows use gpt-engineer output as authoritative input
IF downstream nodes act on that output without human review
IF the workflow includes external side effects such as API calls or file writes
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before downstream actions
Validate A’s outputs against schema or tests
Limit n8n workflows to read-only dry runs first
Log and diff generated artifacts before execution
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source tools with broad filesystem and network surfaces, but the compliance risk depends on what data the n8n workflow processes. Because n8n touches “whatever the workflow processes” and gpt-engineer handles generated source code plus secrets, retention or residency mismatches can arise if regulated data is routed through the pair. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by an n8n workflow that also uses gpt-engineer outputs
IF retention or residency settings differ across the two systems
IF workflow logs or generated files retain sensitive content
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the shared workflow
Set short retention on workflow logs and artifacts
Review data residency for each integration node
Purge generated files after use
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across systems
